CHIEF COMPLAINT
Second opinion regarding right index finger injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Philip Gutierrez is a 50-year-old male who sustained a hyperextension injury to the right index finger during a motor vehicle accident in March 2026 (approximately 3 months prior to this visit). The patient was a passenger in a car that was rear-ended multiple times, which caused him to stretch out his right index finger. He reports the finger felt like it went backwards and has been painful since the accident. He cannot make a fist and describes the pain as sometimes unbearable, even with driving. The finger remains swollen. Prior evaluation at another orthopedic practice included physical therapy and MRI imaging. An MRI obtained on 4/24/2021 showed focal soft tissue swelling over the right index MCP joint, partial-thickness tear of the right flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS), and fluid consistent with tenosynovitis around the FDP and FDS tendons. The radial and ulnar collateral ligaments of the index MCP joint were intact, as was the MCP joint capsule and extensor tendons. The patient was offered an injection of the A1 pulley region but declined due to prior adverse reaction to dexamethasone, which causes his heart to race. He reports confusion regarding treatment recommendations from his prior providers. The patient is right-handed and works as an x-ray technician.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Blood pressure medication (specific agent not specified).

ALLERGIES
Dexamethasone (causes tachycardia).
Methylprednisolone (causes itching).

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as an x-ray technician. He is right-handed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient is a pleasant, cooperative, healthy male in no acute distress. Heart rate regular rate and rhythm with 2+ radial pulse. No swelling or bruising in the palm over the volar surface of the index finger; normal creases slightly diminished over the PIP of the index finger compared to the middle finger. Index finger rests in 10-degree PIP-flexed position. Tenderness to palpation over the PIP joint. Mild decreased sensation noted. Able to bend and straighten the index finger, though with difficulty and reports of tearing sensation. Patient able to make a fist. X-rays of the right hand (four views) show no bony abnormalities, joint congruency throughout all lesser digits, no soft tissue shadows of concern, and no arthritis.

RESULTS
MRI of right index finger (4/24/2021): Focal soft tissue swelling over right index MCP joint, partial-thickness tear of right FDS, fluid consistent with tenosynovitis around FDP and FDS tendons, radial and ulnar collateral ligaments intact, MCP joint capsule intact, extensor tendons intact.
X-rays of right hand today: No bony abnormalities, joint congruency throughout all lesser digits, no soft tissue shadows of concern, no arthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Post-traumatic severe stenosing tenosynovitis of right index finger with partial-thickness tear of flexor digitorum superficialis. Patient has significant scar tissue and inflammation around the FDS tendon blocking excursion of other tendons. Plan includes steroid injection with betamethasone (1 cc) and lidocaine (0.5 cc). Two attempts at trigger finger injection were made with similar technique. First attempt resulted in dramatic painful reaction with hand withdrawal. Second attempt successful with small palmar vein bleeding that was cleaned and bandaged. Patient counseled on importance of therapeutic steroid injection and reassured of no harm to finger. Advised to ice finger this evening and take ibuprofen. Patient instructed to begin active range of motion exercises of the index finger and avoid splinting. Referred for outpatient occupational therapy once weekly for 6 weeks with goal of full active and passive range of motion with no restrictions. Steroid injection expected to improve symptoms within 3-5 days with continued improvement over the next couple of weeks. Patient may require repeat injection. Patient counseled that driving is safe. Follow-up as needed.
